name: C++
summary: Multi-paradigm systems language that grew out of C with classes: deterministic destruction (RAII), templates and concepts, zero-overhead abstractions, and an ISO standard revised every three years (C++11 ... C++26). Implemented independently by GCC, Clang and MSVC.

level_notes.0: No reference implementation: the three major independent implementations are GCC (g++ front end in gcc/cp, libstdc++), Clang/LLVM (clang/, libc++, libc++abi) and MSVC (compiler closed, STL open). Source links point at the main/master/trunk branches and can move as the projects refactor.
level_notes.1: The ISO/IEC 14882 standard is paywalled. The working draft is public: eel.is/c++draft is an HTML rendering of the current draft (now the C++26 working draft) with stable [section.name] URLs; timsong-cpp.github.io/cppwp/nNNNN hosts frozen drafts per standard (n4861 = C++20, n4950 = C++23). WG21 papers (Pnnnn/Nnnnn at open-std.org) are the proposal record. The Itanium C++ ABI is a separate, de-facto binary standard.
level_notes.2: isocpp.org and cppreference.com refuse automated clients from the checking sandbox (reported 'blocked'); their URLs are long-standing and were kept.
level_notes.3: cppreference.com is filed under level 3 (community wiki summarising the standard) although practitioners use it as the everyday reference.
